status_oct_2026.summary: Not completed at 30-Oct-2026. Castrol India's CFO said on 26-Oct-2026 that legal and operational licences across 50+ countries were still being obtained and that the SEBI filing would follow completion. BP's 3Q 2026 results (30-Oct-2026) described closure as imminent and still expected about US$6bn of proceeds in 2026. The DPS has not been published, so the open offer has not opened and there is no acceptance outcome yet.

sebi_sast.points: Open offer for at least 26% on crossing 25% or acquiring control (Reg 3(1), 4, 7(1)); offer price enhanced at 10% p.a. for indirect acquisitions (Reg 8(12)); acquirer may seek delisting through the open offer if intent is declared, for indirect acquisitions initially in the DPS (Reg 5A); an acquirer that crosses the maximum non-public shareholding through an open offer cannot make a voluntary delisting offer for 12 months (Reg 7(5))

sebi_delisting.points: Delisting offer succeeds only if the acquirer's post-offer holding plus accepted shares reaches 90% of total issued shares (Reg 21(a)); counter-offer allowed if holding reaches 75% and at least 50% of public shares are tendered (Reg 22(4), amended 25-Sep-2024); fixed-price route added in 2024

rbi_acquisition_finance.points: Banks were historically barred from lending to buy shares of other companies. RBI's Commercial Banks - Credit Facilities Amendment Directions, 2026 allow bank acquisition finance up to 75% of the acquisition value for eligible acquirers (net worth at least Rs 500 crore, 3-year profit record, investment-grade rating if unlisted, post-deal debt/equity cap of 3:1)

fema_companies_act.points: ECB proceeds cannot be used to buy equity in India; a foreign-owned or controlled Indian company cannot use domestic borrowings to buy shares of another Indian company; Section 67 of the Companies Act 2013 bars a public company from giving financial assistance for the purchase of its own shares
